thread:
maria: quick heads-up — I prototyped a minimal prefix-lease transfer that only moves the lease pointer and leaves residency + tombstone state in the source until explicit demote. wants to land an experiment to see operational behavior.

sam: wait, minimal transfer meaning no data copy at handoff? just pointer swap + soft-demote token?

maria: exactly. idea is: avoid heavy handback during scale events. receiver starts serving reads/writes after pointer swap, but reads fallback to source if missing entry. source keeps residency until demote window expires.

jonah: that sounds risky for read-after-write correctness. what if a write lands on receiver before source applied a recent update?

maria: good call. plan is: receiver accepts writes but forwards a lightweight validation request to source for keys in the demote window. if source has a newer epoch, receiver retries write or proxies. fallback path only for hot keys to keep perf.

priya: forwarding sounds like extra tail latency. how do we avoid amplifying P50?

maria: we only forward on miss or if seqnum mismatch. common case (cached hot key) should stay local. also will add histogram tags to trace forwarded ops.

sam: how does this interact with tombstone compaction? if source retains tombstones longer, receiver might see stale presence and return 404 incorrectly.

maria: tombstones remain authoritative on source until demote completes. receiver reads will treat tombstone as a hint and revalidate. we may need a short TTL for tombstone shadowing to avoid long-lived divergence.

jonah: is this still single-writer per-prefix? lease still enforces single-writer, right?

maria: yes, lease transfer is atomic regarding ownership — the pointer swap happens under the lease service. the trickiness is state residency overlap.

priya: can we express the invariants? i.e., after transfer, (1) receiver must not serve a write that could be lost, (2) reads must not regress older values.

maria: proposed invariants in practice:
- receiver must consult source if local seq < claimed seq or key not found
- writes carry causal token; if source has newer token, write is rejected with E_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT and client retries
- demote completes only after grace window or explicit handback ack

sam: sounds like more of a hybrid protocol. what's the rollout plan? canary + shadow-read opt-in?

maria: yes. rollout: 1) internal opt-in flag for tenant groups, 2) canary on low-traffic shards, 3) shadow-read for 24h with telemetry, 4) enable forwarding for misses only, 5) widen canary.

priya: what metrics do we need from canary?

maria: forwarded_requests_per_second, forward_latency_p50/p95/p99, ownership_conflict_rate, fallback_rate, read_lsa_mismatches, tombstone-bounce-count, and end-to-end application error increase.

jonah: need tests: unit for seqnum checks, integration sim that injects writes during transfer, and a chaos job that kills source mid-demote. also datastore-level regression for tombstone compaction edgecases.

maria: agreed. I'll add an integration harness that replays workload and asserts linearizability for a selection of prefixes.

sam: small nit — add a guard to cap forwarded QPS per node so we don't DDoS source during mass transfers.

maria: yup, will add a token-bucket and backpressure metric.

priya: any change to the public prefix API? clients shouldn't need changes, right?

maria: no client changes. it's internal routing/handshake behavior. only internal admin flags to force demote/abort.

ci-bot: tests queued: prefix-transfer-minimality-unit, seqnum-checks, linearizability-harness. results will post when complete. :gear:

maria: thanks — can everyone review the PR when I post? it includes a small state-machine diagram and a fallback timeline. planning to open tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

sam: will do. add a canary checklist for ops runbook (how to abort and re-route).

jonah: and include a debug command to list tenants in mid-demote and their outstanding forwarded QPS. helps triage.

priya: also confirm billing/metrics tags so cost attribution remains correct during overlap window.

maria: noted. I'll attach telemetry schema and run-level gating controls in the PR.

maria: final question to the group — acceptable demote overlap window? proposing 30s default with exponential backoff up to 5min for retries. thoughts?

sam: 30s default seems reasonable; ops can tune per-cluster.

jonah: OK but stress-test with hot key churn. if we see high conflict rates, reduce window and rely on heavier handback for contentious prefixes.

priya: fine. let's iterate after canary.

maria: great — I'll post PR and link smoke test plan + telemetry dashboard. thanks everyone.
